full_judgment:
3. The contention of the defendant Nos. I and 9 is that the document dated 13-12-14 by Md. Idris in favour of defendant No. 7 relating to schedule 'Ka' property was neither a kot nor a mortgage by conditional sale or a kabala with a condition of purchase, but in fact it was an out and out sale deed and as such the suit was not maintainable in the form presented. On these pleadings the suit was dismissed by the learned Munsif. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed it. Thereafter an appeal was preferred to the High Court which was also dismissed by the Judgment of the learned Single Judge. Against this judgment the plaintiff-appellant preferred a Letters Patent Appeal before a Division. Bench of the Dacca High Court, The Division Bench of the Dacca High Court allowed the appeal and the judgment and decree of the learned Single Judge were set aside. In the Letters Patent Appeal their Lordships held that the transaction was mortgaged by conditional sale and their Lordships were pleased to allow partial redemption of remaining part of the mortgage. Against this judgment and order of the talented Division Bench an application under Order .47, rule 1 was preferred by the defendants and by an order dated 23rd of July, 1968 the same Bench disposing of the Letters Patent Appeal was pleased to issue a Rule calling upon the opposite parties to show cause why the judgment and decree of the Letters Patent Appeal should not be reviewed. 

 In the result, therefore, this rule is made absolute without any orders as to costs and the judgment and decree pissed in the Letters Patent Appeal are set aside. The judgment of the learned Single Judge is hereby restored.
